questions.key_step: Lines symmetric in x,y meet on y=x; distance condition reduces to a+b-c>0.
questions.justification: Routine intersection and distance; the only care is that more than one option can be true. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q1 (L2) in demand; single concept so no MCQ floor.

questions.key_step: d1+d2 = sqrt2*max(x,y) in the first quadrant, so R is a square-frame region.
questions.justification: Needs the modulus simplification |h-k|+|h+k|=2max(h,k) and then a frame-area subtraction; numerical, no options to check. Same kind of region-from-modulus idea as 2021-P1-Q2 (L3).

questions.key_step: Locus is |2x^2-(y-1)^2|=3 lambda^2; chord on y-1=2x gives lambda^2.
questions.justification: Product-of-distances locus (a pair of conjugate hyperbolas) is unusual, and absolute values plus a chord-length condition must be handled precisely. Same stem and level as 2021-P1-Q9 (L4).

questions.key_step: Use lambda^2=9, intersect the bisector with the correct branch, compute R'S'^2.
questions.justification: Builds on Q3's answer, needs the perpendicular bisector and a second chord on the locus; long precise computation. Same stem and level as 2021-P1-Q10 (L5).
